business: Law Office of Mark F. Hughes III
summary: Solo criminal/DWI defence practice run by attorney Mark Fabian Hughes III (NJ bar since 1994), handling DWI and Alcotest refusal, suspended/uninsured driving, CDS, theft/shoplifting, disorderly persons, domestic-violence and juvenile cases out of two rented suites in East Brunswick (Middlesex) and Little Silver (Monmouth). Its entire web presence is a single free Weebly page last modified in 2015: a phone number repeated four times, a dead 'CALL NOW' button, no form, no hours, no booking and no reviews anywhere. The attorney also appears on New Jersey's administrative ineligibility lists in 2024, 2025 and again on the current 2026 Client Protection Fund list, which is a compliance red flag for any engagement.

facts.fact: Site lists the practice areas as DWI and refusal, suspended or uninsured driver, possession of CDS, theft/shoplifting and all disorderly persons cases, domestic violence/harassment, criminal and juvenile cases, and invites a free consultation by phone.

Two office addresses are published: Little Silver Prof'l Plaza, 160 White Road, Suite 204, Little Silver NJ 07739 (Monmouth County) and Williamsburg Commons, 4G Auer Court, 2d Floor, East Brunswick NJ 08816 (Middlesex County).

The page claims 'For over 20 years... hundreds of clients', dismissals in 'a proper case' including Alcotest cases, and prior service prosecuting DWI, criminal and juvenile matters; the site banner also calls him a 'Former Municipal Prosecutor'.

Directory profile records Mark Fabian Hughes III as a Member at Mark F. Hughes III, Esquire, admitted to the New Jersey bar in 1994, Brooklyn Law School J.D. 1993, with 7 listed practice areas including general practice, personal injury, estate planning, real estate, criminal defense, DWI and domestic violence.

Lawyers.com shows 'This firm does not have any client reviews' for the East Brunswick office and 'Not yet reviewed' for the Little Silver office; the Martindale profile shows no client or peer reviews.
The site's sitemap contains exactly one URL (index.html) with lastmod 2015-05-21, and the page is served from a free Weebly subdomain with a 'Powered by Weebly' footer.
Page source has no meta description, no JSON-LD/schema markup, no tel: link and no form; the hero 'CALL NOW (732) 766-5703' button is an anchor with href="javascript:;" (a non-functional button).
The page title is a run-on of name, titles and phone number with no practice area or town: 'MARK F HUGHES III Attorney-at-LawFormer Municipal ProsecutorProtect Your Rights Call (732)766-5703 - Home'.
NJ Lawyers' Fund for Client Protection '2026 NJ Ineligible List For Period Ending November 09, 2026' includes 'Hughes, Mark Fabian', attorney ID 021041994, year admitted 1994.
The same attorney ID (021041994) appears on the Supreme Court's IOLTA 2025 Ineligible List effective September 9, 2025 ('HUGHES MARK FABIAN III'), and on the 2024 IOLTA ineligible list.

Williamsburg Commons on Auer Court is a multi-tenant professional office complex in East Brunswick that houses several small law firms (e.g. Kemeny Ramp & Renaud at 7-G Auer Court, Neal M. Unger PC at 3-E, Law Office of Robert C. Nisenson at 10 Auer Court), with suites in the complex marketed from about 150 sq ft up to roughly 1,650 sq ft.
The only contact channel on the firm's own site is voice telephone (732) 766-5703; no email address, contact form, chat or online scheduler appears anywhere on the page.

inferences.inference: Every enquiry — including after-hours DWI calls — is answered or missed by the attorney personally, with no intake staff or fallback channel.
inferences.reasoning: One named attorney, no staff listed on the site or directories, and the only conversion path is manually dialling a number that is not even a tel: link.

inferences.inference: Missed-call leakage is likely high and invisible, because there is no form, voicemail-to-email or booking option to capture a caller who reaches voicemail at 11pm.
inferences.reasoning: Phone-only intake plus no published hours plus a criminal/DWI caseload whose trigger events (arrests, court dates) happen outside business hours.

inferences.inference: The practice is likely running at low volume or intermittently, and back-office administration is the bottleneck.
inferences.reasoning: Recurring administrative ineligibility on 2024, 2025 and 2026 state lists alongside a website untouched since 2015 and zero reviews — three independent signs that no one is maintaining either the paperwork or the marketing.

inferences.inference: The East Brunswick suite is probably small and possibly shared or part-time rather than a staffed office.
inferences.reasoning: The address is a numbered suite on the 2nd floor of a multi-tenant professional complex where other solos lease small suites; nothing on the site indicates staff or walk-in hours.

inferences.inference: Local search visibility is close to zero, so most new clients would have to arrive by referral or paid directory placement.
inferences.reasoning: No schema, no meta description, a single 2015 page, a free subdomain, and no reviews on any platform found.

inferences.inference: The 'former municipal prosecutor' credential and 'hundreds of clients' claim are unverified marketing statements.
inferences.reasoning: They appear only on the firm's own page; no municipal appointment record, press mention or bar listing was found to corroborate them.

inferences.inference: Any AI or automation engagement should be gated on confirming the attorney's current eligibility to practise.
inferences.reasoning: The most recent state list (period ending 9 Nov 2026) names him, and an ineligible attorney cannot take on new matters until compliance is restored, which would make intake automation pointless in the interim.
